newsitem.title: USA: Union to meet BHP Copper June 24, Chino drags on.
newsitem.headline: Union to meet BHP Copper June 24, Chino drags on.

text.p: The United Steelworkers of America said it will meet BHP Copper on June 24 in a bid to avert arbitration at the former Magma Copper operations in San Manuel and Pinto Valley in Arizona.
"If there is some possibility of doing something then we will find that out on the 24th," USWA lead negotiator Robert Guadiana said.
If there is no deal by the end of June, the stalled labor talks would move to arbitration as agreed within the 15-year framework deal signed by both sides in June 1991.
Every five years, the framework agreement is updated.
The arbitration outcome is binding for a year with no right to strike during that period.
BHP unable to comment immediately on the labor talks.
Meanwhile at Phelps Dodge Corp's Chino mine in New Mexico, Guadiana said the USWA was waiting for the outcome of charges filed against Phelps Dodge with the National Labor Relations Board in Phoenix.

The union had also requested additional information from the company. "I have been provided with some documentation from the company, but nothing more than they are compelled to," Guadiana said. "There are no meetings (with Phelps) scheduled."
Employees at Chino have been working without contracts since June 30 last year, but the mine has been operating throughout this period.
Phelps' Treasurer Tom Foster said he was unaware of any meetings planned with the union at Chino, and confirmed the mine was operating normally. "Things are going well there," Foster said.
